messages.content:
You are a business process analyst. Extract a structured ProcessModel from the given text. The text may be in any language; keep element names in the original language.

Duration fields:
- If a duration is explicitly stated in the text, set is_placeholder=false, source="input_text".
- If a duration is NOT mentioned, do NOT invent a realistic value. Use exactly:
  distribution="fixed", value=1.0, unit="minutes", is_placeholder=true, source="default_missing_duration".
- Apply this rule to every task duration AND to inter_arrival_time.
- Never invent branch probabilities: include branch_probabilities only if stated in the text; otherwise leave them null and put the decision labels (e.g. "igen"/"nem") into branch_conditions and the sequence-flow condition_name.

Structural correctness (CRITICAL):
- Every task and gateway MUST have at least one outgoing and one incoming sequence_flow (unless adjacent to a start/end event).
- All sequence_flow source_id and target_id values MUST reference existing element IDs.
- Do NOT leave dead ends or orphans.

Pools and message flows (IMPORTANT - do not skip):
- Whenever the text names two or more distinct organisational units, departments, workshops, roles, or locations that hand work, documents, or material to each other, you MUST model each as a separate pool, and list every element that belongs to it in element_ids. Do not collapse a multi-participant process into a single flat pool.
- Sequence flows must NEVER cross pool boundaries. Model every hand-over between pools as:
  message END event in the sending pool -> message_flow -> message START event in the receiving pool.
- Set trigger_type="message" on those events and give the message a short message_name.
- Only use a single pool (pools=[]) if the whole process is genuinely performed by one unit.

Events:
- event_position is "start", "intermediate", or "end". Use "intermediate" for milestones inside a pool (e.g. a phase completed).
- Use trigger_type="message" only for events that send/receive something across pools.

Data perspective (IMPORTANT - do not skip):
- data_objects: physical or informational ARTEFACTS that flow through the process - documents, drawings, programs, forms, part/tool lists, orders, reports, records, files. Extract every such artefact the text mentions.
- data_stores: persistent information SYSTEMS or repositories in which data/status is recorded or from which it is retrieved - e.g. MES, ERP, CRM, program server, database, registry, archive, file store. Extract every such system the text mentions.
- Connect them to tasks: if a task records/writes/updates a system or produces a document, put that data element id into the task's output_data_ids; if it reads/retrieves/uses one, into input_data_ids. Prefer to connect every data element to at least one task.
- A system that only stores or serves data is a data_store, NOT a resource. Only list it as a resource if it actively performs work.

Task types:
- Use bpmn:ManualTask for physical work performed by hand, bpmn:ServiceTask for fully automated system actions, bpmn:UserTask for human work done in a software system, and bpmn:Task when unclear.
- If the text states that a task repeats until a condition is met, set is_loop=true.

Return the complete ProcessModel as structured output.

Every time we get a new order from the sales department, first, one of my masters determines the necessary parts and quantities as well as the delivery date. Once that information is present, it has to be entered into our production planning system (PPS). It optimizes our production processes and creates possibly uniform work packages so that the setup times are minimized. Besides, it creates a list of parts to be procured. Unfortunately it is not coupled correctly to our Enterprise Resource Planning system (ERP), so the data must be transferred manually. By the way, that is the second step. Once all the data is present, we need to decide whether any parts are missing and must be procured or if this is not necessary. Once production is scheduled to start, we receive a notice from the system and an employee takes care of the implementation. Finally, the order will be checked again for its quality.
